items.title: RareLens: Towards End-to-End Rare Disease Care via Aligning Divergent Large Language Model Reasoning
items.title_zh: RareLens：通过对齐发散的大模型推理实现端到端罕见病诊疗
items.summary: RareLens reconciles divergent reasoning trajectories from multiple heterogeneous LLMs into decisions across risk screening, diagnosis, treatment planning and prognosis prediction, built on RarelensBench with 157,525 real-world cases spanning 33 Orphanet categories. It outperformed GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet and Gemini-2.5-Pro across all stages, reaching 0.917 AUC for screening and top-1 accuracies of 65.5% and 89.8% for diagnosis and treatment, and in an external evaluation of 1,287 cases with 23 physicians both autonomous and assisted RareLens outperformed unaided physicians.

items.title: Co-Evolving Graph and Text Memory for Training-Free Multi-Hop Question Answering
items.title_zh: 协同演化的图与文本记忆：面向免训练多跳问答
items.summary: Co-E is a training-free system built on synchronized bidirectional graph-text working memory: a synchronization cycle consolidates textual memory, extracts relational triples into graph memory and injects graph facts back into the generation context, so both memories shape subsequent retrieval and generation. On six multi-hop QA benchmarks it improves over comparable training-free open-backbone baselines and is competitive with larger or trained systems.

items.title: AgentOmnia: Scaling Agentic Models for Full-Scenario Applications
items.title_zh: AgentOmnia：面向全场景应用的智能体模型扩展
items.summary: AgentOmnia is a full-scenario agentic scaling framework that coordinates a Domain x Capability x Atomic Difficulty taxonomy with environment-task synthesis, post-training, evaluation and PRD-guided improvement, constructing 5,018 stateful environments, 255,375 tools and 52,361 tasks. Starting from Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507, it raises the OmniaBench challenging-subset pass rate from 9.16% to 37.11% and the four-benchmark macro-average from 22.86% to 41.69%, surpassing Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 on all four benchmarks.

items.title: False Prophets: On the Security of World Models in Agentic Systems
items.title_zh: 假先知：论智能体系统中世界模型的安全性
items.summary: The paper identifies security vulnerabilities specific to learned world models used by LLM agents, showing that attackers can induce mispredictions in terminal-based agent pipelines with up to 95% success, potentially causing unintended command execution, denial of service, wallet drainage and private-information extraction. It introduces a security benchmark dataset for text-based world models and offers practical recommendations for hardening agentic systems.

items.title: An Ontology for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
items.title_zh: 面向机器学习原子间势的本体
items.summary: The paper presents the MLIPs ontology, an OWL 2 DL ontology organized into Method, Training Data and Benchmark modules that describes machine-learning interatomic potential methods, their hyperparameters, DFT-provenance training datasets and published benchmarks. It connects materials-science and machine-learning ontologies, declares 27 formal axioms enforcing data completeness and consistency, and is evaluated through competency questions over a 20-paper seeded knowledge graph and OWL reasoning.

items.title: Beyond a Global Norm: Personalizing Toxicity Sensitivity in Language Models Without Retraining
items.title_zh: 超越全球规范：无需重训练即可个性化语言模型的毒性敏感度
items.summary: The paper compares training-free methods for aligning language generation to individual toxicity sensitivities at pre-decoding, in-decoding and post-decoding stages, evaluated against targets derived from the PRISM dataset. All methods reduced alignment error by 28-47%, but the results reveal a trade-off among alignment effectiveness, personalization and general language quality.

items.title: On the Impossibility of Unbiased and Length-Invariant Policy Optimization with Outcome Rewards
items.title_zh: 结果奖励下无偏且长度不变策略优化的不可能性
items.summary: The paper proves an impossibility theorem showing that, under standard outcome-reward GRPO, no length-based weighting scheme can simultaneously be gradient-unbiased and length-invariant. It characterizes the trade-off with the family f_alpha(L) = L^(alpha-1), where alpha = 0 recovers GRPO and alpha = 1 recovers Dr. GRPO, and shows that Dr. GRPO's length bias can let longer trajectories dominate gradient updates by a factor proportional to the length ratio.

items.title: Confidently Wrong: Exception Chain Collapse in Frontier LLM Rule Evaluation
items.title_zh: 自信地犯错：前沿大模型规则评估中的异常链崩塌
items.summary: The paper documents exception chain collapse, a failure in eligibility evaluation under nested conditional rules, and notes that some failure cells silently closed under the same model alias between March and April 2026. It presents the Aethis Eligibility Module, a neuro-symbolic architecture in which LLMs author rules and an SMT-based layer executes them deterministically, reporting higher accuracy than frontier models on LegalBench tasks.
